doc.title: Lisa Parrott interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 22, 2021

title: Diva Jazz Orchestra and outreach for young women
summary: Diva's Hamilton visit, her leaving in 2015, and Ellen Rowe's outreach group.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Politics, race and the state of the country

blocks.x: Well this has been a fascinating conversation. I’m very glad we did it and I didn’t really ask you too much about the years you spent with the Diva Jazz Orchestra, which we had the group at Hamilton College a number of years ago.
What year was — do you remember what year that was?
It was probably four years ago.
Ah so I’d already left. Yeah I left in 2015.

Yeah. But speaking about reaching out to an audience, it was so inclusive and there was a whole crowd of junior high kids there and they came up on the stage afterwards and I was just watching this whole thing I said this is exactly what we need.

Yes. There’s another group I play with too that Ellen Rowe at the University of Michigan started in 2017 mainly because she’s been teaching there for twenty years and there’s still not enough young women going into improvised music at college and at the high school level as well so she formed together a group to do outreach and we’ve had to put plans on © Fillius Jazz Archive -17-

hold but we are going to be doing some stuff in January. Great group. We did a recording in 2017 so Ellen, Marian, in Detroit, oh my God, I’m having a mental blank. Bass player from Detroit, oh my gosh. Oh that’s terrible. Allison Miller on drums, the front line Ingrid Jensen, Virginia Mayhew, Tia Fuller and Melissa on trombone. Sorry. I haven’t seen these people for a while, I’m forgetting everyone’s last names.
And you’re fourteen hours away, it’s okay.

So, and I did experience that with Diva. It’s like they need to see women up on stage, young men and women need to see mixed bands, all women bands, they need to see bands like this, that’s what’s going to create a really, a much more inclusive scene and music teaches people how to be good citizens a lot, that’s what I believe as well. And you know I’m very proud of the outreach stuff that we did with Diva and also with this other group. Yeah.
